reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about configurational entropy, lattice distortion, and diffusion barriers, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific nanoparticle behavior claimed, so the lack of cited support leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: High configurational entropy lowers the free energy of the disordered phase in multi-element nanoparticles
Lattice distortion in these nanoparticles creates kinetic barriers to elemental diffusion
Suppressed diffusion and phase segregation are the primary mechanisms for kinetic stabilization at high temperature
A reduction in configurational entropy (off-equiatomic composition) lowers these kinetic barriers
Near-equiatomic nanoparticles will therefore better preserve single-phase structure than off-equiatomic ones under high temperature
